issues.legal_issue: The claimants did not prove that the disputed land was the same land acquired at auction and subsequently leased to them.
material_facts: The claimants relied on an auction purchase and later leases to establish their rights to the disputed land.
The defendants expressly denied in their pleadings that the auction purchaser had acquired the disputed land.
The auctioned land was described as lying on one side of a river in a different district and state from the disputed land, which lay on the other side.
Although the land was subject to river action, the claimants did not produce cogent evidence connecting the disputed land to land submerged by the river.
issues.conclusion: The claimants failed to prove that the disputed land was the land acquired at auction and later leased to them; their appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: A claimant relying on an acquisition and subsequent transfer must prove that the land claimed is the same land covered by those transactions. Where a river's action is relied on to connect land in a new location to the land originally acquired, the burden of proving that connection rests on the claimant.

rule.if: land_title_claim and identity_of_claimed_land_denied and land_location_change_attributed_to_river and identity_evidence_insufficient

predicates.land_title_claim: A claimant brings a land-title claim relying on an earlier acquisition and a subsequent transfer of the land.
predicates.identity_of_claimed_land_denied: The opposing party denies that the land claimed is the land covered by the earlier acquisition and transfer.
predicates.land_location_change_attributed_to_river: The claimant relies on river action to explain why the claimed land is located somewhere different from the land described in the acquisition.
predicates.identity_evidence_insufficient: The evidence does not cogently connect the claimed land to the land covered by the earlier acquisition.

issues.definition: When a land-title claim depends on identifying land said to have shifted location through river action, the claimed identity is not proved if the opposing party denies it and the evidence does not cogently connect the two locations.

issues.legal_issue: A remand was not warranted where the request rested on an unfounded assumption that the identity of the land had not been disputed and would prolong litigation that had already continued for many years.
material_facts: The claimants requested a remand to present further evidence, saying they had believed the defendants did not dispute the identity of the land.
The defendants had expressly denied that the auction purchaser acquired the disputed land in their written pleadings.
The suit had been filed more than twenty-five years before the remand request, and many original parties had died and been replaced by legal representatives.
A remand would have required another round of trial and appeal proceedings.
issues.conclusion: The Court rejected the request for remand and dismissed the appeal. It relied on the absence of a valid basis for the claimants' assumption and the need to bring the protracted litigation to an end.
issues.legal_principle: Courts should not prolong old litigation by remanding a case where the asserted reason for needing further evidence has no valid basis in the record, particularly when remand would extend a long-running dispute into succeeding generations. The Court reiterated the approach in Sant Narain Mathur v. Rama Krishna Mission, AIR 1974 SC 2241.

rule.if: civil_appeal_seeking_remand and remand_request_based_on_unfounded_assumption and litigation_protracted and remand_would_prolong_dispute

predicates.civil_appeal_seeking_remand: A party in a civil appeal asks the court to send the case back for further proceedings.
predicates.remand_request_based_on_unfounded_assump: The stated reason for seeking remand is an assumption contradicted by the pleadings or other record in the case.
predicates.litigation_protracted: The dispute has already continued for many years, with original parties having died and being represented by successors.
predicates.remand_would_prolong_dispute: Sending the case back would require further trial or appellate proceedings and extend the dispute.

issues.definition: A remand is denied when a civil appeal seeks it on a premise contradicted by the record and further proceedings would prolong an already long-running dispute.
